subject: Food Science
title: Biofilms on Surfaces
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Biofilms on Surfaces.

hook.text: That slimy film inside a water bottle? It's a biofilm—a fortress of bacteria glued together with self-made slime.

buildup.text: Bacteria attach to surfaces and secrete a sticky matrix called extracellular polymeric substances. Colonies form fast.

discovery.text: Biofilms are 1,000 times more resistant to sanitizers than free-floating bacteria. Scrubbing is often the only solution.

twist.text: Food factory pipes, cutting boards, and drain covers are biofilm hotspots. They recontaminate food after cleaning.

climax.text: Listeria biofilms in deli slicers have caused deadly outbreaks. Equipment design now targets biofilm prevention.

punchline.text: Bacteria build cities on surfaces. Sanitizer alone won't tear them down.

quiz.question: How much more resistant are biofilms compared to free-floating bacteria?
